output.summary: Deterministic verdict preserved: the run is VALID with COMPLETE coverage, and capacity is BOUNDED with lower_inclusive 197 and upper_exclusive 297 users. Step-1 (target 100) and step-2 (target 200) PASSed with window latency response_time_p95_ms = 140 (threshold 250); step-3 (target 300) FAILed because the window latency policy check observed response_time_p95_ms = 420 > 250, giving verified_bound_load 297. The overall capacity policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT because capacity_knee is null (knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED). Observed error_count is 0 across 3601 samples; overall latency p95/p99/max are 417/420/1500 ms. Load-generator CPU stayed about 0.43 mean (max 0.45) in all three stages, below the generator-cpu guard threshold 0.85, but the generator-cpu summaries are identical across windows. clock_alignment is "not_verified_by_core". The advice below tests the capacity-boundary location, the tail-latency cause, generator CPU instrumentation, clock alignment, and measurement representativeness; it does not change the verdict.

hypotheses.observation: capacity_summary step-3 (target 300 users) has verdict FAIL with achieved 297 verified_bound_load (p05_10s), matching the window latency policy check where observed response_time_p95_ms = 420 > threshold 250; stages 1 and 2 passed with observed 140.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: At roughly 297-300 concurrent users the system breached the 250 ms p95 latency SLO while it was within SLO at ~197 users, suggesting a capacity threshold between the last pass (197) and the observed fail (297).
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run a fine-grained load ramp between ~197 and ~297 users (e.g., ~25-user steps) with the same latency policy and stable-window duration to locate and confirm the transition point.

hypotheses.observation: The stage-3 window showed response_time_p95_ms = 420 (FAIL) while error_count is 0 and error_rate_ratio is 0/3601 for both overall and checkout; the overall summary reports p99 420 ms and max 1500 ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The failure is a tail-latency SLO breach rather than an error-rate breach; a minority of slow samples (max 1500 ms, p99 420 ms) could be driving the elevated p95 at ~300 users.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the per-window and per-sample latency distribution in stage-3 (histogram, samples near 1500 ms, count of samples above 250 ms) to determine whether the breach is broad degradation or a small slow tail.

hypotheses.observation: The generator-cpu guard policy checks PASSed in all three stages (observed max ratio 0.45 vs threshold 0.85) while latency still degraded in stage-3.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Load-generator CPU saturation is an unlikely cause of the stage-3 latency increase; the cause may lie in the system under test, network, or a backend, but no server-side metrics were collected in this run to confirm.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect server-side CPU, memory, GC, queue, DB, and network metrics while repeating the 300-user stage to localize where contention or queuing occurs.

hypotheses.observation: The generator-cpu resource summaries are identical across all three windows (mean 0.43, max 0.45, same sample_standard_deviation, iqr 0.02, same slope_per_second).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The CPU series may have been statically repeated or not actually sampled per window, so the conclusion that the generator was not saturated is not fully verified.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify the raw generator-cpu series for each window and the collector instrumentation to confirm distinct per-window sampling before relying on generator-resource conclusions.

hypotheses.observation: resource-binding reports clock_alignment "not_verified_by_core" and uses explicit_windows with 30 cells per stage and no dropped cells.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without verified clock alignment between load generation and the system under test, ordering a load increase before a latency change cannot support a temporal causal claim.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization (e.g., NTP offsets) across load generator, collector, and system under test before performing any lead/lag or causality analysis.

hypotheses.observation: capacity_summary has capacity_knee null with knee_reason "KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED", policy_verdict "NO_VERDICT", and bounds lower_inclusive 197 / upper_exclusive 297.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The analysis verifies a pass at ~197 users and a fail at ~297 users but does not compute a precise knee, so the capacity verdict remains NO_VERDICT rather than a completed capacity determination.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Enable knee detection or add intermediate load steps so a capacity knee can be computed and a policy verdict issued instead of NO_VERDICT.

hypotheses.observation: Overall throughput is about 4 rps (numerator 3601000 / denominator 900500) across 3601 samples, while active_users reached ~297-300 in stage-3.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: With a low per-user request rate and only ~1200 samples per stage, the stage-3 latency percentiles may not reflect a heavier request mix; the 197-297 user boundary could shift under different think times.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compare the achieved request rate and think-time profile with the intended production mix, and re-run with representative request rates to confirm the capacity boundary.

hypotheses.observation: metric-summary-overall and the metric summary for transaction "checkout" report identical values (sample_count 3601, p95 417, p99 420, max 1500), and no other transaction summaries appear in the evidence.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The traffic may be entirely checkout requests, or other transaction types were not summarized, so conclusions may apply only to the checkout path.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm the JMeter run's sample labels and separately summarize any other transaction types so endpoint coverage is explicit.

recommendations.action: Run a fine-grained load ramp between ~197 and ~297 users (e.g., ~25-user increments) using the same latency SLO and stable-window duration.
recommendations.rationale: The last verified pass was at 197 users (step-2) and the first observed FAIL at 297 users (step-3, p95 420 ms > 250 ms), so the boundary sits between these points but is not precisely located.

recommendations.action: Add server-side resource and service metrics (CPU, memory, GC, queue depth, DB, network) alongside the load-generator metrics during the 300-user stage.
recommendations.rationale: Only load-generator CPU was captured and it stayed far below the 0.85 guard, so the cause of the latency increase must be tested outside the generator.

recommendations.action: Verify clock synchronization (e.g., NTP offsets) across load generator, collector, and system under test before any lead/lag or causal claims.
recommendations.rationale: resource-binding reports clock_alignment "not_verified_by_core"; without verified clocks, temporal ordering between load increases and latency degradation is unsupported.

recommendations.action: Analyze the stage-3 latency tail: inspect the sample histogram around the 250 ms threshold, the samples near the 1500 ms max, and the count of samples above 250 ms.
recommendations.rationale: Stage-3 p95 is 420 ms against a 250 ms threshold, with overall p99 420 ms and max 1500 ms; distinguishing broad degradation from a small slow tail changes the likely cause.

recommendations.action: Verify the generator-cpu metric instrumentation: confirm each window produced an independently sampled CPU series.
recommendations.rationale: The generator-cpu summaries are identical across all three windows (mean 0.43, max 0.45, same standard deviation), suggesting possible static or duplicated data.

recommendations.action: Treat the 197-297 user interval as indicative and re-run with knee detection enabled or more granular steps so a capacity point and policy verdict can be issued.
recommendations.rationale: policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT and capacity_knee is null with knee_reason "KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED"; the current result is a bounded pass/fail range, not a completed capacity determination.

recommendations.action: Confirm that the think-time/request-rate profile is representative of production before acting on the 197-297 user boundary.
recommendations.rationale: Overall throughput is about 4 rps (3601000/900500) across 3601 samples for up to ~300 users, so latency percentiles rest on a low per-user request rate that may not match production load.

caveats: policy_verdict is NO_VERDICT and capacity_knee is null (knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED); the pass/fail bounds are indicative, not a completed capacity determination.
Only one failing load point was observed (verified_bound_load 297 from a target of 300); the exact transition between 197 and 297 users was not measured.
No server-side resource metrics were collected, so no cause for the stage-3 latency increase (p95 420 ms > 250 ms) is established.
clock_alignment is "not_verified_by_core"; temporal ordering or causality between load changes and latency is not verified.
The generator-cpu series is identical across all three windows, suggesting possible instrumentation or static-data issues; generator stability is not fully verified.
metric-summary-overall and the checkout transaction summary are identical (sample_count 3601), and no other transactions are summarized; conclusions may apply only to the checkout path.
error_count is 0 across observed loads; absence of errors does not prove stability or spare capacity.
Total throughput is about 4 rps (3601000/900500) with 3601 samples; p95/p99 percentiles are computed over a small sample count relative to 300 users.
The window summaries report resource_verdict NO_POLICY for all stages; absence of a resource policy is not equivalent to a resource-health pass.
run_validity VALID and analysis_coverage COMPLETE describe data coverage, not the correctness of a capacity conclusion.
